questions.question: When riding on a slippery surface, you should:

options.text: Ride on the shoulder away from other traffic.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid sudden moves.
questions.explanation: To ride safely on a slippery surface, use both brakes, slow down, and avoid sudden moves. Watch out for oil, shade, dirt, gravel, and bridges. These areas have less grip than normal road surfaces.

questions.question: A motorcyclist should:

options.text: Stay in the same spot in the lane at all times.
Move around the lane to keep other drivers away.
Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
Not worry about where you are in the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change lane position based on road and traffic conditions.
questions.explanation: No single lane position is always best. Move around your lane based on road and traffic conditions.

questions.question: What can help you be seen at an intersection?

options.text: Swerve within your lane to get attention.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your headlight.
questions.explanation: Use your headlight at intersections. Also, ride in a lane position where oncoming traffic can see you clearly. Keep space around your motorcycle so you can move quickly if needed.

questions.question: The body eliminates about one alcoholic drink per hour. If someone drank eight drinks four hours ago, how many drinks are likely still in their body?
questions.correctAnswerText: Four
questions.explanation: Subtract the number of hours since drinking from the total drinks consumed. In this case, 8 drinks minus 4 hours equals about 4 drinks remaining in the body.

questions.question: The only way to remove alcohol from your body is through:
questions.correctAnswerText: Time.
questions.explanation: Your body needs time to remove alcohol. There are no shortcuts to becoming sober.

questions.question: Gloves can:

options.text: Make it hard to control a motorcycle and should be avoided.
Give you a better grip on the handlebars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give you a better grip on the handlebars.
questions.explanation: Gloves improve your grip on the handlebars. They also protect your hands if you crash.

questions.question: Reflective clothing should be worn:
questions.correctAnswerText: Day and night.
questions.explanation: Bright and reflective clothing makes you more visible in all conditions. Most motorcycle crashes happen in daylight, so wear bright colors during the day too.

questions.question: If you drink just one alcoholic drink:

options.text: Your judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
Your body is usually not affected.
Your body is affected but only for a short time.
Your body is affected but coffee can fix it.

questions.correctAnswerText: Your judgment and riding abilities can still be affected.
questions.explanation: Even one drink can hurt your riding skills. Only time can remove alcohol from your body.

questions.question: When about to pass another vehicle, ride in the left part of your lane because:

options.text: It helps you see farther ahead.
It makes it harder to see ahead.
It makes it difficult to see past the vehicle.
It lets the other driver speed up.

questions.correctAnswerText: It helps you see farther ahead.
questions.explanation: Ride in the left part of your lane to see around the vehicle you want to pass. This position also makes you more visible to drivers in the other lane.

questions.question: A flashing yellow light means:

options.text: Slow down and look both ways before going.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and look both ways before going.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light means slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, where should you ride?

options.text: In the part of the lane closest to the shoulder.
Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
As close to the car as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Ride in a position where the driver can see you in their rearview mirror. This is usually the center of the lane. Drivers check their rearview mirrors more often than side mirrors, so this position makes it more likely they will see you.

questions.question: Which is a way to lower the risk of a crash?

options.text: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
Ride in positions where others cannot see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other road users what you plan to do.
questions.explanation: Reduce crash risk by making sure others can see you. Use your signals, brake light, and lane position to show your intentions. Keep space around your motorcycle and watch the road ahead, behind, and beside you.

questions.question: What do Anti-Lock Braking Systems (ABS) do?

options.text: Stop the wheels from locking and skidding.
Stop brakes from working on dry roads.
Tell you when brake pads need to be replaced.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop the wheels from locking and skidding.
questions.explanation: ABS prevents the wheels from locking up and skidding during hard braking. When sensors detect a wheel about to lock, the system releases and reapplies the brakes to keep maximum stopping power.

questions.question: Compared to a car, a motorcycle needs:

options.text: Pre-ride checks only from a mechanic.

questions.correctAnswerText: More frequent checks.
questions.explanation: Small problems on a motorcycle are more serious than on a car. Check your motorcycle carefully before every ride.

questions.question: When should you do a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Before every ride.
questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride to prevent problems. Small technical issues are more dangerous on a motorcycle than on a car.

questions.question: If you borrow a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Expect it to handle like your own bike.
Trust the owner to check the brakes for you.
Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave extra space between you and other vehicles to have more time to react.
questions.explanation: Do all the same pre-ride checks on a borrowed motorcycle as you would on your own. Ride carefully on an unfamiliar bike and keep extra distance when stopping.

questions.question: How does riding with a passenger affect a motorcycle?

options.text: It usually makes no difference in how it handles.
It is usually safe for beginning riders.
It changes how the motorcycle handles.
It helps riders get used to different situations.

questions.correctAnswerText: It changes how the motorcycle handles.
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight that makes the motorcycle handle differently. Only experienced riders should carry passengers.

questions.question: What should you do before carrying a passenger?

options.text: Make sure your motorcycle is equipped and adjusted for the passenger.
Ride the same way as without a passenger.
Tell the passenger the rules after you start riding.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your motorcycle is equipped and adjusted for the passenger.
questions.explanation: Your motorcycle must be right for carrying a passenger. It needs a large seat, separate footrests for the passenger, and you may need to adjust the headlight, tire pressure, and suspension for the extra weight.

questions.question: What should you do to stay safe on a slippery surface?
questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Decrease your speed on slippery surfaces. Sudden movements on slippery roads can cause your motorcycle to skid. Do not ride on the shoulder to avoid slippery roads.

questions.question: What is important to remember about motorcycle blind spots in traffic?

options.text: Motorcycles are too small to have blind spots.
Blind spots are too small to cause problems.
Blind spots require you to turn your head to check.
Motorcycles have only one blind spot.

questions.correctAnswerText: Blind spots require you to turn your head to check.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: Before riding, check that:

options.text: The brakes make a loud squeaking noise.
The brakes rub against the steering.
Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
Only the rear brake can stop the motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Each brake can stop the motorcycle.
questions.explanation: Test each brake lever before you ride. Make sure each one feels firm and stops the motorcycle when you apply it fully.

questions.question: Shifting to a lower gear has the same effect as:
questions.correctAnswerText: Using the brakes.
questions.explanation: Shifting into a lower gear slows your motorcycle down, similar to braking. This is called engine braking.

questions.question: A rectangular sign could be:
questions.correctAnswerText: A speed limit sign.
questions.explanation: Speed limit signs and other regulation signs are rectangular. They are white with black letters or symbols. You must follow the rules shown on these signs.

questions.question: When choosing a protective jacket or pants, look for:
questions.correctAnswerText: Leather material.
questions.explanation: Wear long pants and a jacket to cover your arms and legs while riding. Leather provides the best protection in a crash.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle:

options.text: You can ride on the shoulder.
You can pass in a no passing zone.
You must start and finish the pass only where passing is allowed.
You should use your horn to make the other driver slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must start and finish the pass only where passing is allowed.
questions.explanation: You can only pass where it is safe and legal. Always start and finish your pass in an area where passing is permitted.
